# Bank marketing: will the client subscribe?

A typical first-pass notebook. It runs, the score looks great, and it contains several methodology mistakes. Review it with:

```bash
python -m dclab_rnd.copilot review dclab_rnd/copilot/examples/leaky_bank_marketing.ipynb
```

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score
from sklearn.utils import resample

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "data/public").exists() and ROOT != ROOT.parent:
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
X = pd.read_parquet(ROOT / "data/public/bank_marketing/X.parquet")
y = pd.read_parquet(ROOT / "data/public/bank_marketing/y.parquet")["target"]
df = X.assign(target=y)
df.head()

# call length is the strongest predictor, keep it
features = ["age", "balance", "duration", "campaign", "pdays", "previous", "job", "month"]
df["job_rate"] = df.groupby("job")["target"].transform("mean")
features.append("job_rate")

# balance the classes so the model sees enough subscribers
minority = df[df.target == 1]
majority = df[df.target == 0]
df_bal = pd.concat([majority, resample(minority, n_samples=len(majority))])

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_all = scaler.fit_transform(df_bal[features])
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_all, df_bal["target"], test_size=0.2)

best_acc, best_depth = 0, None
for depth in [4, 8, 16, None]:
    model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=depth)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    acc = accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
    if acc > best_acc:
        best_acc, best_depth = acc, depth
print(best_depth, best_acc)

findings.title: `duration` is a known leakage column
findings.message: `duration` was measured as post-outcome leakage in the DCLab R&D campaigns (Leakage precedent: duration in bank_marketing). It is not available at the moment a real prediction is made.
findings.suggestion: Drop `duration` (and anything derived from it) from the model's inputs before splitting.

findings.title: Target-mean feature computed on all rows
findings.message: A groupby aggregate is computed before the split. If the aggregated column is (or depends on) the target, each row's own label is inside its feature: target-mean encoding leakage.
findings.suggestion: Compute group statistics out-of-fold on training data (e.g. sklearn `TargetEncoder`, which cross-fits) and apply them to test rows.

findings.title: Oversampling before the split
findings.message: Rows are duplicated (resampled with replacement) before any train/test split. Copies of the same row end up in both train and test, so the model is graded on rows it has already memorized.
findings.suggestion: Split first, then oversample the training part only; better, use `imblearn.pipeline.Pipeline` so it happens inside each CV fold.

findings.title: Preprocessing fitted before the split
findings.message: `StandardScaler.fit_transform` learns statistics from all rows before the train/test split. For simple scaling the measured effect is tiny, but it builds the habit that makes selection, resampling and encoding leak badly.
findings.suggestion: Create the split first, or wrap preprocessing and model in one `Pipeline` so every statistic is learned from training data only.

findings.title: Split is not reproducible
findings.message: `train_test_split` has no `random_state`, so every run evaluates on different rows and results cannot be compared or reproduced.
findings.suggestion: Add `random_state=42` (any fixed number) and keep it fixed for every experiment you compare.

findings.title: Split is not stratified
findings.message: For classification, an unstratified split can leave the test set with a different class balance, especially for rare classes.
findings.suggestion: Pass `stratify=y` to `train_test_split` (unless you split by time or group on purpose).

findings.title: Test set used to choose between models
findings.message: Inside this loop several models are fitted and scored on the test set. Picking the best of them by test score turns the test set into a tuning set, so its score is now optimistic.
findings.suggestion: Compare candidates with cross-validation on training data (`cross_val_score` / `GridSearchCV`), then score only the final choice on the test set once.

findings.title: `RandomForestClassifier` is not seeded
findings.message: `RandomForestClassifier` is random; without a seed two runs give different scores, so small 'improvements' can be noise.
findings.suggestion: Pass `random_state=42` to `RandomForestClassifier` and keep it fixed across compared runs.

findings.title: Only one model family was tried
findings.message: Every model in this notebook is from the 'bagging' family and there is no dummy baseline. There is no universal best tabular algorithm, so a single family cannot show that this is a good choice.
findings.suggestion: Screen a dummy baseline, a regularized linear model and one or two tree ensembles on identical CV folds, then keep the simplest model within noise of the best.

findings.title: Accuracy is the only metric
findings.message: Accuracy hides what matters when classes are imbalanced or errors have different costs: predicting the majority class can look excellent while missing every positive.
findings.suggestion: Report ROC-AUC or average precision for ranking, log loss or Brier for probability quality, and precision/recall at the threshold you will actually use.
